key_insight: NeFTY represents the 3D thermal diffusivity as a continuous neural field and couples it with a differentiable heat-diffusion solver to recover quantitative interior material properties from transient surface temperatures, overcoming limitations of pixel-wise 1D approximations and fragile PINN training in transient diffusion.
problem_solved: Accurate, quantitative 3D reconstruction of material diffusivity from transient surface thermography measurements while accounting for lateral heat diffusion and enabling stable gradient-based inversion.
method: Parameterize the 3D thermal diffusivity as a continuous neural field (neural implicit representation) rather than per-pixel 1D models.
Integrate a differentiable transient heat-diffusion forward solver so gradients from surface temperature mismatch backpropagate to the neural field for end-to-end inversion.
Use this differentiable physics pipeline to stabilize training in transient diffusion problems and produce volumetric material-property reconstructions from surface measurements.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable, physics-aware approach to solve inverse thermal problems and non-destructive evaluation tasks, enabling higher-fidelity volumetric reconstructions and more reliable gradient-based optimization than conventional thermography or soft-constrained PINNs.
